symptom: After ako/mxcli#1790, adding one attribute to one entity still made the incremental source rebuild describe every entity of its module and every document that used any of them: 346 of 3,718 documents for an unreferenced entity in a 154-entity module
cause: The reuse basis was the unit, and an entity is not a unit: it lives in its module's domain model, so the domain model's hash stood for every entity in it, and the dependents query was seeded with all of their names
insight: **Pick the basis by what the describe reads, not by the storage unit.** `describeEntity` reads only the entity's own subtree (attributes, rules, indexes, handlers and access rules are all inside it; associations are not printed), so the subtree hash is a sound basis and the rest of the domain model becomes a parent whose change still re-describes the module. Raw BSON is the right thing to hash: element order is stored order, so hashing the array element bytes is deterministic without a canonical form. Observing *which* documents were described (a nil-by-default hook on the describe func) is what makes the control bite: comparing rows with a full build passes with the coarse basis too, since over-describing is never wrong, only slow
fix: Hash each entity's subtree (plus its domain model's ID, so a move between modules is a change) under the entity's own ID, hash the domain model without `Entities` under the unit's ID, and make the domain model each entity's parent in the plan. Test: `TestSourceCatalog_IncrementalBuildEqualsFullBuild` asserts the sibling entity is carried over; with `entityBasis` stubbed out it fails naming the sibling
